title: Auto Scaling
subtitle: Target-tracking vs queue-depth scaling, predictive pre-warming, oscillation damping, and cold-start mitigation.
keyTakeaways: Scale stateless tiers on leading work indicators (queue depth per worker, active concurrent requests) rather than lagging host metrics like memory or raw CPU alone.
Asymmetric cooldown windows (fast scale-out in 30-60s, conservative scale-in over 10-15m) prevent thrashing and premature termination of warm instances during bumpy traffic.

Reactive auto-scaling is too slow for sudden flash crowds (e.g., ticket drops or push notifications) because container image pull + JVM/app boot + cache warmup takes 60-180 seconds—requiring Predictive or Scheduled pre-scaling.

sections.heading: Scaling Control Loops, Signals, and Thrashing Prevention
sections.body: Auto-scaling dynamically adjusts compute capacity to match demand through a closed-loop proportional controller: $\text{Desired Replicas} = \lceil \text{Current Replicas} \times (\frac{\text{Current Metric}}{\text{Target Metric}}) \rceil$. Choosing the right control signal determines whether the controller stabilizes or oscillates.
bullets: Why Memory Is a Poor Scale-In Metric: Managed runtimes (JVM, Go, Node.js) rarely return freed heap pages to the OS immediately; scaling on memory causes the cluster to scale out to max replicas and never scale back down.
Queue-Based Event-Driven Scaling (KEDA): For async workers, scale based on `queue_backlog / acceptable_processing_rate_per_worker` so backlog drain time stays constant regardless of spike size.

Asymmetric Stabilization Windows: Scale out aggressively as soon as demand spikes, but enforce a 10-to-15-minute stabilization cooldown before scaling in, draining existing in-flight connections gracefully (`SIGTERM` + `preStop` sleep).

codeSnippet.title: Kubernetes HPA v2 with Asymmetric Scale-Up/Scale-Down Behavior
codeSnippet.code:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: checkout-api-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: checkout-api
  minReplicas: 12
  maxReplicas: 200
  metrics:
    - type: Pods
      pods:
        metric:
          name: http_requests_per_second
        target:
          type: AverageValue
          averageValue: 500
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
      policies:
        - type: Percent
          value: 100
          periodSeconds: 30
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600
      policies:
        - type: Percent
          value: 10
          periodSeconds: 60

sections.heading: Cold-Start Lag, Overprovisioning Headroom, and Downstream Backpressure
sections.body: When a pod scales out, if the underlying Kubernetes cluster has no spare node capacity, provisioning a new cloud VM takes 45-90s, pulling container images takes 15-30s, and warming JIT/connection pools takes another 15s.
bullets: Pause-Pod Overprovisioning (Headroom Buffer): Run low-priority 'pause/balloon pods' that reserve 15% spare node CPU/RAM. When real production pods scale out, they immediately preempt the pause pods in <2 seconds while Karpenter provisions new VMs in the background.

Predictive & Scheduled Scaling: Use historical diurnal traffic patterns (or pre-scheduled cron rules before marketing push notifications / live sports events) to pre-scale capacity 15 minutes ahead of the wave.

Protecting Non-Scalable Bottlenecks: Scaling stateless app pods from 20 to 200 (each opening 20 DB connections) suddenly demands 4,000 Postgres connections, crashing the database! Always cap `maxReplicas` or place a connection pooler (PgBouncer/RDS Proxy) in front of stateful stores.

tradeOffs.pros: Zero manual intervention; adapts organically to organic diurnal curves and unexpected traffic shifts.
tradeOffs.cons: Lags behind instantaneous flash spikes by 1-3 minutes (cold start window), risking initial 503 drops.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Standard web APIs, microservices with gradual organic traffic growth, and background consumer pools.

tradeOffs.pros: Sub-second pod scheduling into warm spare node capacity; handles vertical flash-crowd spikes cleanly.
tradeOffs.cons: Pays continuously for 10-20% idle 'balloon' node buffer capacity.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Flash sales, live streaming events, ride-hailing surge windows, and push-notification backends.

interviewTip: Always warn about the 'Auto-Scaling Database DoS' in interviews: horizontally auto-scaling your stateless tier 10x will immediately exhaust database connections and melt your stateful tier unless you enforce connection pooling and hard concurrency limits.
